CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep negotiating a limited settlement that trades additional US goods purchases and bounded IP/market-access language for a lasting freeze—and preferably a path to roll back—List 3, without accepting a unilateral US snap-back enforcement mechanism that would permanently weaponize tariffs. Do not raise new retaliatory duties or widen the Meng/Canada confrontation while talks are live; keep Huawei legally separate from the trade text and hold the existing retaliation schedule as residual leverage until Washington commits in writing on the 10%→25% hike and the $50B duties.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not high/existential. Combined US Section 301 coverage is still ~$250B (Lists 1–2 at 25%, List 3 at 10% from 24 Sep 2018), and Huawei remains a national-champion/tech-sovereignty hit: DOJ unsealed fraud/sanctions charges on 28 Jan 2019, Canada authorized the extradition case to proceed on 1 Mar, and a May 8 hearing was set. Export-hub stress is documented (official PMI 49.4 in Dec 2018, first contraction in over two years; Dec exports −4.4% y/y). That sits below the +0.5 CHN anchor because the immediate List 3 hike was suspended at the 1 Dec G20 dinner, delayed again by Trump on 24 Feb, and allowed to lapse on 1 Mar; CNY strengthened from ~6.97 (late Oct) to 6.7064 on 13 Mar; reserves rose to ~$3.12T; and seasonally adjusted merchandise exports rebounded in March. Action should stay near zero, not escalate: Lighthizer told the Senate Finance Committee on 12 Mar that “major issues” remain, success is unpredictable, and China is pushing for full tariff removal while the US wants unilateral proportional enforcement—so a new Chinese tariff or non-tariff blast would give Washington a pretext to restore the 25% List 3 hike. Nor is concede_purchases/full_rollback warranted: there is still no matching US offer to lift existing duties, and binding structural/enforcement language as Lighthizer described (regular meetings plus US unilateral action if unresolved) would constrain industrial policy. Negotiate—purchases as a sweetener, core industrial-policy red lines intact—is the stance that uses the open channel (Lighthizer/Mnuchin still on continuous calls as of 11–13 Mar) without paying for a deal that does not yet exist.
key_factors: List 3 still at 10% on ~$200B after G20 truce and Feb 24/Mar 1 delay; $50B remains at 25%
Talks advanced on purchases but enforcement, IP/tech transfer, SOE subsidies still open as of Lighthizer 12 Mar testimony
Huawei/Meng legal track escalating (DOJ charges; Canada ATP 1 Mar; May 8 hearing) while formally kept off the trade table
Export/factory slowdown in late 2018 (PMI contraction; Dec export drop) but FX, reserves, and March trade/IP readings are not crisis-like
US wants unilateral snap-back enforcement; China wants existing tariffs removed—no matching rollback offer yet

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: Trump and Xi agree to a 90-day negotiation window. Planned Jan 1, 2019 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% is suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
Trump tweets that talks have made substantial progress and further delays the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; US formally requests Meng's extradition from Canada.
Another round of talks (through Feb 15). Progress reported on purchases; enforcement mechanism still disputed.
CNY/USD 6.7064 on 2019-03-13, stronger vs ~6.97 late-Oct peak (−2.15% over the window); not a depreciation crisis.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.118T on 2019-03-01, up ~$45B over the window.
US customs imports from China fell from $52.1B (Oct 2018) to $31.1B (Mar 2019), −40%—bilateral export channel is already compressed.
Lighthizer told Senate Finance on 12 Mar 2019 that major issues remain unresolved, he cannot predict success, China is pushing for all US tariffs to be removed, and enforcement design is still open.
USTR suspended the List 3 10%→25% hike until further notice; Lighthizer insists on structural changes plus US ability to act proportionally but unilaterally.
Official manufacturing PMI 49.4 in Dec 2018, first contraction since July 2016; new export orders shrank a seventh straight month.
Canada authorized the US extradition case against Meng to proceed; Beijing called it a serious rights violation and continued to hold Kovrig and Spavor.
